description: Hydrogenation/dehydrogenation energy balance for LOHC (DBT) and Ammonia carriers
source: Niermann et al. (2021) Energy Environ. Sci.; Preuster et al. (2017) Acc. Chem. Res.; Lamb et al. (2019) Int. J. Hydrogen Energy

gravimetric_capacity_wt_pct.note: H2 content by mass of DBT carrier. Niermann et al. 2021

delta_H_hydrogenation.note: Enthalpy of hydrogenation (exothermic, negative). Preuster et al. 2017: 65 kJ/mol

delta_H_dehydrogenation.note: Enthalpy of dehydrogenation (endothermic, positive). Preuster et al. 2017

T_reactor_hydrogenation_K.note: Typical hydrogenation temperature 150°C. Preuster et al. 2017

T_reactor_dehydrogenation_K.note: Typical dehydrogenation temperature 300°C. Preuster et al. 2017

molar_mass_carrier_kg_per_mol.note: Molar mass of H0-DBT (fully dehydrogenated). Bruckner et al. 2014

H2_mol_per_mol_carrier.note: 9 H2 molecules per DBT molecule (H18-DBT). Preuster et al. 2017

energy_efficiency_dehydrogenation.note: Fraction of ΔH supplied as heat that drives reaction; rest = losses

gravimetric_capacity_wt_pct.note: H2 content by mass of NH3. 3 H2 per NH3. Lamb et al. 2019

delta_H_synthesis.note: Enthalpy of NH3 synthesis per mol H2 consumed (exothermic). Lamb et al. 2019

delta_H_cracking.note: Enthalpy of NH3 cracking per mol H2 produced (endothermic). Lamb et al. 2019

T_reactor_synthesis_K.note: Haber-Bosch synthesis temperature ~450°C. Lamb et al. 2019

T_reactor_cracking_K.note: NH3 cracking temperature ~500°C. Lamb et al. 2019

energy_efficiency_cracking.note: Fraction of ΔH supplied as heat that drives cracking
